name: Anjar
description: Anjar is an eighth-century Umayyad city in Lebanon's Bekaa Valley, close to the Syrian border. Caliph Walid I founded it, and its ruins still show a strikingly orderly grid of streets, much like the palace-cities of antiquity. Today the surrounding town is home almost entirely to Armenians, so a visit pairs early Islamic urban planning with a living community.
